what_it_does: Running a large language model (AI chatbot) on very long documents is slow and memory-hungry for two reasons: first, the attention mechanism — the part that lets the model look back at everything it has read so far — gets quadratically more expensive as the text grows longer; second, the model must keep a running memory of past context (called a key-value cache, a table of compressed notes about every word seen so far) that can grow enormous. Traditional compression techniques that round numbers to fewer decimal places (quantization) break down here because a few unusually large values (outliers) in the cache corrupt accuracy, and decompressing on the fly costs extra time. MILLION applies a technique called product quantization — splitting each cache entry into sub-vectors and compressing each sub-vector separately — with special handling for outliers, plus a custom GPU program (a low-level routine that runs in parallel on thousands of GPU cores) that keeps decompression asynchronous so it does not stall computation.
